contexts.text: The pleasures of honours and of offices in the commonwealth. AC 995:2.
On those who had been... useless in the commonwealth.
Charity thus... wishes well to others, and to the commonwealth itself...
Natural good is then all delight and pleasure from the spiritual end of serving the neighbour, still more the commonwealth...
Society, the commonwealth, and the kingdom would go to ruin without these laws...
It is as in a city, commonwealth, or kingdom...
After the love of dominion had destroyed this commonwealth (of the most ancient times)...

Dignities are natural and temporary when a man regards himself in them, and not the commonwealth and uses; for then he cannot but think inwardly that the commonwealth exists for the sake of him, and not he for the sake of the commonwealth... But the same dignities are spiritual and eternal when a man regards himself as to person for the sake of the commonwealth and uses.
Those things which are of the commonwealth, and are called civil things, have a place below the former ones...
To shun evils because they are hurtful... to the commonwealth... To do goods because they are profitable... to the commonwealth... He shuns the evil of adultery as the pest... of the commonwealth...
The Dutch pretended that they so act for the sake of their Republic...
As mankind are distinguished into empires, kingdoms, and republics...
Wherefore, in a well-constituted commonwealth no one is allowed to be useless...
Of these four things the commonwealth or society consists. Char 135.
